title: fix(sdui-parser): the base-prop list is declared once, and the renderer's visibleWhen / hiddenOn / testId join it (objectui#11044)
body:
Fixes #11044
Clause-②: yes

Seat `domain:ui#2`, PM session `https://claude.ai/code/session_011p7ikEivgXefNDaE5S5Uec`, branch `claude/issue-11044-base-props-one-list` (PM claim `5885808433`). Direction per triage `5883977635`: one list, members 1 to 3, with member 2 as triage ruled it.

## What this changes

`validateTree` kept a `BASE_PROPS` set, and `generateDts` kept a separate hand-written `SduiBaseProps` interface. They were two lists of the same thing, and they had drifted. The validator had 11 entries and the interface had 8. The interface lacked `type` (on purpose, because the tag name carries it), plus `hidden` and `bind`. So after PR objectui#11042 the validator accepted `bind` and `hidden` on every node, while the generated JSX types still refused both.

- `packages/sdui-parser/src/validate.ts`: a new exported `SDUI_BASE_PROPS` is the one list. Each entry gives a `BaseSchema` member, a scope and the attribute's TypeScript type. `BASE_PROPS` (the `every-node` members) and a new `WHERE_UNDECLARED_BASE_PROPS` are derived from it. The name `BASE_PROPS` is kept because prose in other packages cites it.
  - **Member 1.** `visibleWhen`, `hiddenOn` and `testId` join as `every-node` members.
  - **Member 2 (triage ruling).** `name`, `label`, `description`, `placeholder`, `data` and `ariaLabel` join as `where-undeclared` members. The loop skips one of them only when the type declares no input of that name. Where one is declared, the declared input's lookup runs, `type-mismatch` included.
- `packages/sdui-parser/src/codegen.ts`, **member 3.** The `SduiBaseProps` interface is emitted from `SDUI_BASE_PROPS` (every entry except `type`). A component that declares a `where-undeclared` member extends an `Omit` of `SduiBaseProps` over the keys it declares, so its declared type wins, as it does in the validator. Without the `Omit`, a declared type the base type does not admit is a TS2430 on the generated file. Reverse-verification leg D below measures this.
- `packages/sdui-parser/src/index.ts`: exports `SDUI_BASE_PROPS`, plus the `SduiBaseProp` and `SduiBasePropScope` types.
- `packages/sdui-parser/scripts/gen-manifest.ts` is not edited. It calls `generateDts`, so it follows. The generated files are not committed: `buildArtifacts` has no caller in this repo, and `scripts/` is not in the package's `files`. What ships is `generateDts` itself, which is what the `tsc` pin compiles.
- `.changeset/11044-base-props-one-list.md`: `minor` for `@object-ui/sdui-parser` (an accept set widens, and there are new exports).

Values of existing entries are unchanged. The `every-node` members that some registrations do declare (`className`, `disabled`, `id`, `visible`) still skip their declared lookup, as before. See the acceptance notes.

## Pins

- New `packages/sdui-parser/src/__tests__/base-props-one-list-11044.test.ts` (54 tests), against a synthetic manifest:
  - the generated `SduiBaseProps` block equals the list, entry for entry;
  - every entry draws nothing on a node that declares nothing, and four near-misses (`testid`, `visibleIf`, `hiddenWhen`, `aria-label`) still draw one `unknown-prop`, which is the lit control;
  - member 2: for each of the six keys, a type that declares it answers `424242` with `type-mismatch`, and a type that does not declare it draws nothing;
  - member 3: an in-memory `tsc` program over the generated `.d.ts` plus a page, mapped one statement per line. The `.d.ts` itself has zero diagnostics. A `list` element accepts `bind`, `hidden`, `visibleWhen`, `hiddenOn`, `testId` and an undeclared `label`, and refuses `bindTo`. A `field` element that declares `data` as an array refuses an object `data` (the declared type wins), while `list` accepts it (the base type is `unknown`).
- New `packages/components/src/renderers/__tests__/base-props-one-list-11044.test.tsx` (4 tests), against the live registry of that package:
  - every list entry is a key of the `BaseSchema` zod shape, and `body` is the one member left out;
  - no registration declares `visibleWhen`, `hiddenOn` or `testId`, and none of the three draws a diagnostic naming it on any registered type;
  - for each `where-undeclared` key, every declaring registration keeps its type check and every other registration draws nothing naming the key.
- `packages/sdui-parser/src/__tests__/base-props-bind-hidden-11008.test.ts`: the `placeholder` row's prose said the key "stayed OUT of the set". It now says `placeholder` is a `where-undeclared` member, and that the row goes red if the key is made `every-node`. The assertions are unchanged.

## Fixture triage: consumer controls this change falsified

The consumer radius (every test importing `@object-ui/sdui-parser`, plus every test naming `unknown-prop`, `generateDts` or `SduiBaseProps`) had four red rows. Each one pinned exactly the branch member 2 moves:

- `examples/schema-catalog/test/pageheader-with-actions.test.tsx`: the lit control added `description` to a `page-header`. That key is the retired alias of `subtitle` (objectui#3226, and the renderer stopped reading it in objectui#3789). The control now uses the near-miss `subTitle`. A new row pins that `description` now draws nothing there. This is the named cost of the ruling, so restoring the warning later has to be a deliberate change.
- `packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/detailSectionAuthoredHideEmpty-10485.test.tsx` and `detailSectionAuthoredIcon-9529.test.tsx`: the lit control was `name`, a `DetailViewSection` member the block neither declares nor reads. It is now `hideIfEmpty` and `iconName` respectively. No `DetailViewSection` member can serve any more: the block leaves out only `name` and `visible`, and both are base props now.
- `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/__tests__/dashboardAuthoredInputs.test.tsx`: `dashboard` declares `label` and `description`, so its interface now extends the `Omit` over those two keys. The regex reads that. Every per-key assertion is unchanged.

## Measurements

Census through a temporary vitest probe, deleted after use and never committed. It loaded `@object-ui/components`, `@object-ui/fields` and all 19 `plugin-*` packages, `plugin-tree` by source path, so the registry held **519** known types. The card's probe loaded fewer plugin packages and read 488. The probe built the manifest with `manifestFromConfigs` and ran `validateTree` once per key per type, first with a well-typed value and then with `424242`. Before is `480de81fd` (the base). After is this branch.

| key | registrations declaring it | types naming the key, well-typed value: before, after | `424242`: before, after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `visibleWhen` | 0 | 519 `unknown-prop`, then 0 | 519 `unknown-prop`, then 0 |
| `hiddenOn` | 0 | 519, then 0 | 519, then 0 |
| `testId` | 0 | 519, then 0 | 519, then 0 |
| `placeholder` | 25 | 494 `unknown-prop`, then 0 | 494 `unknown-prop` + 25 `type-mismatch`, then 25 `type-mismatch` |
| `name` | 13 | 506, then 0 | 506 + 13, then 13 `type-mismatch` |
| `label` | 50 | 469, then 0 | 469 + 50, then 50 `type-mismatch` |
| `description` | 55 | 464, then 0 | 464 + 55, then 55 `type-mismatch` |
| `data` | 29 | 490 `unknown-prop` + 11 `type-mismatch`, then 11 `type-mismatch` | 490 + 29, then 29 `type-mismatch` |
| `ariaLabel` | 2 | 517, then 0 | 517 + 2, then 2 `type-mismatch` |

Every declared `type-mismatch` survives, and no existing member's row moved. The 11 `data` rows after the change are declarations of `object` or `code`, which answer the probe's array value with a mismatch, as a declared input should.

`tsc` probes (`strict`, no `skipLibCheck`):

- The card's probe (`generateDts` over a `list` with `title` and `items`, then a page). Before: `bind`, `hidden`, `visibleWhen`, `hiddenOn`, `testId` and `label` each give TS2322, and the declared control compiles. After: all of them compile. An added `bindTo` gives TS2322 with the hint "Did you mean 'bind'?".
- `generateDts` over the real published manifest (`getPublicConfigs()` over the console's registration graph, 107 types). Before: one error, TS2430 on `RecordAlertProps` (see the acceptance notes). After: the same one error and no new one. 15 interfaces now extend the `Omit`. The file diff is 41 lines: 11 new `SduiBaseProps` members, and 15 changed `extends` lines.

## Tests and gates

The union ran after the final commit, at HEAD `5b0996905`:

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/sdui-parser/` (20 files) plus the consumer radius (73 files: every test importing `@object-ui/sdui-parser`, every test naming `unknown-prop` / `generateDts` / `SduiBaseProps`, and the new components pin): **93 files, 1593 tests passed**.
- Eight changeset-state suites in `scripts/__tests__` (`check-changeset-*`, `changeset-polarity-census`, `check-pending-changeset-literals`, `check-control-bytes`): **8 files, 330 tests passed**.
- Gates at HEAD, each exit 0: `check-changeset-presence`, `check-control-bytes`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-pending-changeset-literals`, `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` (0 new). `check-governed-queue-guard --test` over the 11 paths answers NOT GOVERNED.
- `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 10 changed code files gives 10 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, and none ignored. `eslint.config.js` sets no type-aware parser options, so this diff cannot move the verdict on an untouched file.
- `type-check` exits 0 for `sdui-parser` and `components` (after `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/components^...' build`), and for `plugin-detail`, `plugin-dashboard` and `example-schema-catalog` (after their dependency closures were built). `tsc --listFilesOnly` confirms that each package's test program holds the new or edited test files.
- Also exit 0: `check:phantom-deps`, `check:self-import`, `check:esm-specifiers`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check-changeset-claims` (report-only; the three pending bodies it names describe `manifestFromConfigs` in `index.ts`, which this change does not touch).
- NOT MEASURED: `check:readme-exports`. It needs every package built, and on this tree it reports that its population collapsed. `@object-ui/sdui-parser` has no README.

Declared narrowing: the full `pnpm test`, the repo-wide `pnpm lint` and the full type-check farm are CI's.

## Reverse verification

Each leg is one-off and committed-first. It uses objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (the anchor must hit, and the blob change is checked), inside a script whose `EXIT INT TERM` trap restores the file. After each leg the file's blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty. The root vitest alias maps `@object-ui/sdui-parser` to its `src`, so each mutation reached the tests without a build. Each leg ran five files: both new pins, the 11008 sdui-parser pin, the dashboard pin and the schema-catalog pin.

1. **A, delete the `visibleWhen` entry.** Anchor count 1 to 0, blob `7cc3d76d4634` to `d2f4a57962a7`. Result: **6 failed, 103 passed**. Red rows: the list-coverage row, the `visibleWhen` accept row, the member-1 row, the `tsc` row, and in components the `BaseSchema` row and the all-registrations row.
2. **B, make `placeholder` `every-node`.** Blob to `f1d3a62400f0`. Result: **3 failed, 104 passed**. Red rows: the "six members" row, the `.d.ts` compile row (the `FieldProps` `Omit` string lost `placeholder`), and the 11008 `placeholder` type-check row. The member-2 `it.each` rows did not go red, because their population is derived from the list and shrank with it. The rows that pin the population caught the change.
3. **C, delete the `where-undeclared` skip line.** Blob to `aebc57218748`. Result: **14 failed, 95 passed**. Red rows: all six undeclared-case rows in both describe blocks, the components row, and the schema-catalog `description` row. The declared-case rows stayed green.
4. **D, drop the `Omit`.** Blob `ac39892e6250` to `36fc417b089d`. Result: **2 failed, 107 passed**. The `.d.ts` compile row received "Interface 'FieldProps' incorrectly extends interface 'SduiBaseProps'. Types of property 'label' are incompatible". The dashboard regex row went red too.
5. **E, codegen drops `bind` from its emission.** This is a second list in effect. Blob to `c4e5d1eab555`. Result: **2 failed, 107 passed**. Red rows: the `SduiBaseProps` equality row, and the `tsc` row for `bind`.
6. **F, cross-package type.** In the components pin, `'where-undeclared'` was changed to `'where-undeclard'`, and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` ran for `components` against the rebuilt `sdui-parser` dist. Result: `TS2367 … the types 'SduiBasePropScope' and '"where-undeclard"' have no overlap`, exit 2. The test program reads the rebuilt `.d.ts`. A first attempt at F quoted the lock command wrongly, and the wrapper refused it as a usage error before running anything. That was a no-op, not a measurement, and it was restored at once.

The direction was red in every leg, as predicted before each run.

## For the objectstack save-gate port (objectstack-ai/objectstack#20578)

The port carries three things: `SDUI_BASE_PROPS`, the `where-undeclared` skip line in `validateTree`, and the list-driven `SduiBaseProps` / `Omit` emission in `codegen.ts`. No diagnostic code is added or removed. `acceptsChildren`, `CHILD_LIST_KEY` and the containment `if` are untouched, so the lockstep record's containment-predicate closure does not move.

## Acceptance notes

- **The cost of member 2, named.** On a type that does not declare one of the six keys, the parser tier no longer reports it, whether or not that type's renderer reads it. The measured instance is the one above: `description` on `page-header`, a retired alias that no renderer reads, used to draw `unknown-prop` and now draws nothing. How many undeclaring types actually read each key is NOT MEASURED (no census of read sites).
- **The generated `.d.ts` over the published manifest already fails `tsc` before this change, and still does.** `record:alert` declares `visible` as boolean, string or object, while `SduiBaseProps.visible` is `boolean`, which gives TS2430 on `RecordAlertProps`. `visible` is an `every-node` member, so this change does not `Omit` it. Fixing it needs a decision about declared `every-node` members (below), so it is not fixed here.
- **Declared `every-node` members keep their silenced type check, as before.** In the 519-type census, `className` is declared by 227 types, `disabled` by 24, `id` by 12 and `visible` by 1. Applying member 2's lookup to them would not be mechanical. `disabled` is declared `boolean` by those 24, while `SchemaRenderer` evaluates a predicate `disabled` for every node, so a declared-first check there would flag values the renderer honours. This is left as it was.
- **The JSX surface types `visible`, `disabled` and `hidden` as `boolean`,** while `BaseSchema` also admits a predicate. `hidden` follows its two siblings, and each has a string predicate partner in the list (`visibleWhen` / `visibleOn`, `hiddenOn`, `disabledOn`).
- **Out of scope, per triage:** a deprecation warning for `visibleOn` against the canonical `visibleWhen`.
- **Docs:** no docs page or README describes the parser's base props. `@object-ui/sdui-parser` has no README, so none was edited.
